steps.title: Set up a reaction profile
steps.body: In Reaction Profiles, use Add Profile to create one and give it a clear name with Rename Profile if needed. Read Active Reaction Profile to confirm which profile is in use. Speaking style shapes how the persona reacts. Delete Profile is available when a profile is no longer wanted; removing one affects only that profile.

steps.title: Define a reaction rule
steps.body: In Reaction Rules, use Add Rule and read Reaction rule, Enabled, Action, Strictness, Emotion override, Repeat mode, and Nth match interval. Keep one simple rule for a first test so its effect is easy to read. Remove Rule deletes the rule. Disable it with Enabled rather than deleting when you only want to pause it.

steps.title: Understand how strictness and repeat mode interact
steps.body: Strictness decides how closely copied content must match before a rule fires. Repeat mode with Nth match interval governs repeated matches. A rule that seems never to fire may be too strict; one that fires too often may need a longer interval. Adjust one control at a time.

steps.title: Read the advanced prompt before editing
steps.body: Advanced Prompt Rules holds the instruction template for reactions. Read the current text first, since prompt changes affect every reaction. If you need to undo changes, Restore recommended prompt returns the suggested template. Use Review Prompt Preview to see the resulting prompt before relying on it.
steps.target_hint: This control may depend on available content or a loaded addon. Read the step here; no service or provider is enabled by the guide.

steps.title: Use the prompt preview as a check
steps.body: Press Review Prompt Preview after any edit to see how the template reads. The preview shows the prompt text, not a live reaction, so it is a formatting check rather than proof the addon will respond. If the preview looks wrong, restore the recommended prompt and edit again with a smaller change.
